newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS GET WAKE-UP CALL-TEICHMANN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS GET WAKE-UP CALL-TEICHMANN.

text.p: Springbok captain Gary Teichmann said on Friday recent poor performances by South African provincial sides had rung alarm bells for the world champions ahead of their test series against the British Lions.

"The fact that some of our sides have gone off the boil a little in the Super 12 has given us a bit of wake-up call -- that we're not as good as we make out to be and that we must start working together," Teichmann said.
Natal are currently the best placed South African team in the southern hemisphere competition, lying in third place, but they have not won in their last four outings.
The Lions, under manager Fran Cotton, depart London on Saturday for a three-test series and 10 provincial matches.
"The Lions are going to be a good side and there's no way we can sit back and say the northern hemisphere are not up to standard with the southern hemisphere," said Teichmann.

"I believe that it's going to be a very hard test series but I believe that we've got the players to win. If we don't have too many injuries and if we can maintain the same sort of core that we had last year, then it'll go well."
After the disappointment last year of losing a home series to New Zealand for the first time, South Africa bounced back with five successive test wins against Argentina, France and Wales.
Teichmann proved to be an inspirational and focused captain who always led from the front.
This year, Teichmann has been in storming form at number eight for Natal and he believes the Lions' strength lies in their forwards.
"I think their pack is going to be strong -- they've got in a couple of their league players and they've got good lineout forwards. So we can expect a very hard tussle up front," he said.

"With their backline players, again they've brought in a few league players who are tough customers. They've adapted to the union game quickly -- most of them played union before and then came back, so it's not a big change for them. But, all-round, I think the Lions will be a good side."
With the Lions party grouping together players from the four Home Nations, Teichmann is aware the initial challenge facing experienced coach Ian McGeechan is settling on a test lineup.

"That'll be the key factor -- if they can sort out their test side from their weekday side and how soon they can get it together. But they're all top players so they should be able to do it fairly quickly.
"What's good for them is that they've got a long period playing against the provincial sides before they play us in the tests so they would have had a few games to sort things out."
